problem: Removing historical Guadalcanal/Solomons fighting changes both material wear and individual amphibious experience; these effects point in opposite directions.

material_wear.LST_LCI_LCVP_LCM: Some South-Pacific hull/engine/beaching wear is avoided, but Branch Santo/New Caledonia and ongoing logistics consume part of the saving. Use only a small 0 to +5 percent serviceability effect before local combat losses, not extra hulls by fiat.
material_wear.LVT: Guadalcanal itself creates almost no direct LVT inventory credit because the large tracked-assault system matured later. Tarawa and 1944 production/training are the dominant LVT gates.

crew_experience.APA_boat_coxswains_and_landing_control: Potentially slightly less individually battle-seasoned than historical because repeated Solomons amphibious operations are absent/altered.
crew_experience.staff_doctrine: Tarawa is longer and more costly in the Branch, so institutional lessons on wave control, reserve LVT, wreck removal, direct fire and repair are at least historical-equivalent and in some areas stronger.
crew_experience.LVT_units: Rapid expansion still dilutes trained crews; preserved Tarawa amtrac survivors provide a somewhat healthier experienced cadre, but do not erase new-unit training friction.

net_model.raw_material_serviceability: 0 to +5 percent relative historical where the same hull/unit can be traced
net_model.individual_boat_crew_experience: roughly historical to modestly worse in units whose historical experience came mainly from Solomons
net_model.system_level_amphibious_process: historical-equivalent to modestly better after Branch Tarawa learning
net_model.rule: Never combine these into one blanket multiplier. Apply to distinct failure modes: mechanical availability, navigation/control, traffic congestion, recovery, and fire-support coordination.
